nodes.title: Fundamental Theorem of Integral Calculus
points: Statement: If f(x) is continuous on [a, b] and ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + c, then ∫_a^b f(x) dx = [F(x)]_a^b = F(b) − F(a).
The arbitrary constant 'c' cancels out: (F(b) + c) − (F(a) + c) = F(b) − F(a).
Geometrical meaning: ∫_a^b f(x) dx represents the algebraic (net signed) area under curve y = f(x) from x = a to x = b.
Substitution in Definite Integrals: When substituting t = g(x), ALWAYS change limits of integration: at x = a ⟹ t = g(a); at x = b ⟹ t = g(b).

formulas.label: Net signed area
formulas.expr: Area above X-axis (+) , Area below X-axis (−)

nodes.title: Definite Integral as Limit of a Sum
points: Definition: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = lim_(n → ∞) h ∑_(r=1)ⁿ f(a + rh), where step size h = (b − a)/n.
Standard conversion of summation series into definite integral:
Step 1: Express series in form lim_(n → ∞) (1/n) ∑_(r=1)ⁿ f(r/n).
Step 2: Replace r/n by x, replace 1/n by dx, replace lim ∑ by ∫.
Step 3: Limits of integration: Lower limit = lim_(n → ∞) (1/n) = 0; Upper limit = lim_(n → ∞) (n/n) = 1.
Result: lim_(n → ∞) (1/n) ∑_(r=1)ⁿ f(r/n) = ∫₀¹ f(x) dx.

formulas.label: Limit of sum definition
formulas.expr: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = lim_(n → ∞) h ∑_(r=1)ⁿ f(a + rh)

nodes.title: Basic Properties (P1 to P4)
points: Property 1 (Zero width): ∫_a^a f(x) dx = 0.
Property 2 (Reversing limits): ∫_a^b f(x) dx = −∫_b^a f(x) dx.
Property 3 (Dummy variable): ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(t) dt = ∫_a^b f(u) du (value is independent of integration variable).
Property 4 (Splitting interval): ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^c f(x) dx + ∫_c^b f(x) dx (where a < c < b).
Crucial for Modulus Functions: To integrate |x − c| from a to b, split at x = c.

formulas.label: P4 (Splitting)
formulas.expr: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^c f(x) dx + ∫_c^b f(x) dx

nodes.title: King's Property (The Master Property)
points: Property 5 (King's Rule): ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(a + b − x) dx.
Property 6 (Special King's Rule with a = 0): ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a − x) dx.
How to apply King's Property:
Step 1: Let I = ∫_a^b f(x) dx ... (1).
Step 2: Apply property: I = ∫_a^b f(a + b − x) dx ... (2).
Step 3: Add (1) and (2): 2I = ∫_a^b [f(x) + f(a + b − x)] dx.
Step 4: Often integrand simplifies to 1, giving 2I = b − a ⟹ I = (b − a)/2.

formulas.label: King's Property (a to b)
formulas.expr: ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(a + b − x) dx

nodes.title: Even and Odd Functions Property
points: Property 7 (Symmetric Limits −a to a):
1. If f(x) is an EVEN function [f(−x) = f(x)]: ∫_(−a)^a f(x) dx = 2 ∫₀^a f(x) dx.
2. If f(x) is an ODD function [f(−x) = −f(x)]: ∫_(−a)^a f(x) dx = 0.
Examples of Even functions: cos x, x², x⁴, |x|, sec x.
Examples of Odd functions: sin x, tan x, x³, x, ln[(1 − x)/(1 + x)].
Product rule: (Even × Odd = Odd); (Odd × Odd = Even); (Even × Even = Even).

formulas.label: Even function rule
formulas.expr: ∫_(−a)^a f(x) dx = 2 ∫₀^a f(x) dx (if f(−x) = f(x))

nodes.title: Periodicity & Half-Upper-Limit Properties
points: Property 8 (Double limit 0 to 2a):
∫₀^(2a) f(x) dx = 2 ∫₀^a f(x) dx (if f(2a − x) = f(x)).
Periodic Property: If f(x + T) = f(x) (periodic with fundamental period T):
1. ∫₀^(nT) f(x) dx = n ∫₀^T f(x) dx.
2. ∫_a^(a + nT) f(x) dx = n ∫₀^T f(x) dx (independent of lower limit a!).
3. ∫_(nT)^(mT) f(x) dx = (m − n) ∫₀^T f(x) dx.

nodes.title: Modulus & Piecewise Integrals
points: To evaluate ∫_a^b |f(x)| dx:
1. Find roots of f(x) = 0 that lie strictly within (a, b). Let root be c.
2. Split integral: ∫_a^b |f(x)| dx = ∫_a^c |f(x)| dx + ∫_c^b |f(x)| dx.
3. On sub-intervals where f(x) ≥ 0, replace |f(x)| by +f(x).
4. On sub-intervals where f(x) < 0, replace |f(x)| by −f(x).
5. Integrate each piece and add results.

formulas.label: Modulus splitting
formulas.expr: ∫_a^b |x − c| dx = ∫_a^c −(x − c) dx + ∫_c^b (x − c) dx

nodes.title: Walli's Formula & Log Sine Integral
points: Walli's Formula for ∫₀^(π/2) sinⁿx dx = ∫₀^(π/2) cosⁿx dx:
where k = π/2 if n is EVEN, and k = 1 if n is ODD.
The Famous Log Sine Integral (Board Classic):
∫₀^(π/2) ln(sin x) dx = ∫₀^(π/2) ln(cos x) dx = −(π/2) ln 2 = (π/2) ln(½).
∫₀^π ln(sin x) dx = 2 ∫₀^(π/2) ln(sin x) dx = −π ln 2.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Proofs
points: Board Favourite #1: Theorem: Prove that ∫_a^b f(x) dx = ∫_a^b f(a + b − x) dx.
Board Favourite #2: Theorem: Prove that ∫₀^a f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(a − x) dx.
Board Favourite #3: Theorem: Prove that ∫_(−a)^a f(x) dx = 2 ∫₀^a f(x) dx (even) and 0 (odd).
Board Favourite #4: Theorem: Prove that ∫₀^(2a) f(x) dx = ∫₀^a f(x) dx + ∫₀^a f(2a − x) dx.
Board Favourite #5: Evaluate: I = ∫₀^(π/2) [√sin x / (√sin x + √cos x)] dx = π/4 (4 marks).
Board Favourite #6: Prove that ∫₀^(π/2) ln(sin x) dx = −(π/2) ln 2.

formulas.label: Proof: King's property
formulas.expr: Substitute t = a + b − x ⟹ dt = −dx

nodes.title: MHT-CET 5-Second Definite Hacks & King's Shortcuts
points: King's Master Shortcut: For ANY integrand where f(x) + f(a + b − x) cancels to 1:
Examples solvable in 2 seconds:
1. ∫₀^(π/2) [sinⁿx / (sinⁿx + cosⁿx)] dx = (π/2 − 0)/2 = π/4 (for ANY power n!).
Odd Function Zero Hack: If limits are symmetric (−a to a) and integrand is odd, answer is ZERO instantly! (e.g., ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2) x³ cos x dx = 0).
